items.question: Can any experience be entirely free from auspicious and inauspicious qualities?
premises: Auspicious and inauspicious must be experienced
Nothing is anywhere devoid of them
items.inference: All experience necessarily contains both auspicious and inauspicious aspects
items.plain_english: Auspicious and inauspicious things must be experienced, and nothing is ever devoid of them anywhere.

items.question: What mental state brings liberation to a practitioner in this life?
premises: A person may possess the transcendent mind
Such a mind transcends ordinary mentation
items.inference: One whose mind becomes transcendent attains liberation here
uncertainties: bhavantīha may be read as bhavati iha with sandhi
items.plain_english: But for one whose mind has become transcendent, liberation arises here.

items.question: Does the liberated person remain affected by sin and merit?
premises: Liberation may arise for such a person
Sin and merit ordinarily bind beings
items.inference: The liberated person is not tainted by sin or merit
uncertainties: bhavedyastu is a fused form; exact segmentation uncertain
items.plain_english: For him there may be liberation, and he is not stained by sin or merit.

items.question: How certain and unattached is the liberation of such a person?
premises: Liberation is affirmed for that person
A water drop does not cling to a lotus leaf
items.inference: His liberation is beyond doubt and unattached like a drop on a lotus leaf
items.plain_english: For him there is liberation, without doubt, like a drop of water on a lotus leaf.

items.question: What event at the fall of the body marks the final release?
premises: The fall of the body occurs at death
A specific rupture is described at that moment
items.inference: At the body's fall, when the skull is pierced, that moment is decisive
uncertainties: kapālambhidyate is a fused form; internal sandhi noted
items.plain_english: O Goddess, when at the fall of the body the skull is pierced, then...

items.question: Which chapter concludes with the topic of emergence in the moon island?
premises: The text is organized into chapters
This section is identified by number and topic
items.inference: This marks the end of the thirteenth chapter on the installation emerged in the moon island
uncertainties: candradvīpavinirgate may refer to a prior topic rather than nyāsa
items.plain_english: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, concerning what has emerged in the moon island.

items.question: What supreme method grants accomplishment immediately without wheel meditation?
premises: Wheel meditation is a known practice
A method exists that is free from it
items.inference: There is a supreme method, free from wheel meditation, that immediately brings accomplishment
items.plain_english: There is a supreme method, free from wheel meditation, that immediately brings accomplishment.

items.question: What wondrous teaching is the goddess invited to hear next?
premises: The speaker addresses the goddess directly
The teaching is described as wondrous and astonishing
items.inference: The goddess is asked to hear a wondrous teaching that produces great astonishment
uncertainties: tvamadbhutaṃ is a fused form; internal sandhi noted
items.plain_english: Hear, O Goddess, this wondrous teaching that causes great amazement.

items.question: Which classes of beings are included among those seeking or affected by this teaching?
premises: Various celestial and powerful beings are listed
Ascetics are included among them
items.inference: Gandharvas, kinnaras, yakshas, asuras, and ascetics are all involved
uncertainties: garndhavāḥ appears to be a nonstandard spelling of gandharvāḥ
items.plain_english: Gandharvas, kinnaras, yakshas, asuras, and ascetics.

items.question: What kinds of unqualified recipients lack devotion to kula and guru?
premises: Devotion to kula is required
Devotion to the guru is required
items.inference: Those devoid of devotion to kula and deprived of devotion to the guru are unqualified
items.plain_english: Indeed, in one who is devoid of devotion to the kula and deprived of devotion to the guru.

items.question: What negative traits characterize those who revile truth and are unfit recipients?
premises: Certain moral and intellectual faults are listed
Reviling truth is a disqualifying trait
items.inference: Deceivers, the miserable, the deluded, and the deficient who revile truth are unfit
uncertainties: hīnāni may agree with an implied neuter noun
items.plain_english: Deceivers, the miserable, the deluded, and the deficient, in one who reviles truth.

items.question: What consequence follows if a teacher gives this teaching to unfit disciples?
premises: A teacher may give the teaching to such disciples
Spiritual accomplishment depends on proper transmission
items.inference: If the teacher gives it to these disciples, accomplishment is lost
uncertainties: dadyāstu is a fused form; syntax is compressed
items.plain_english: If a teacher should give this to such disciples, his accomplishment is diminished.

items.question: What balanced qualities should characterize a worthy recipient of the teaching?
premises: Steady delight in dharma is valued
Freedom from empty anger is valued
items.inference: A worthy recipient is always devoted to dharma and free from empty anger
uncertainties: rataye and krodhaye forms are unusual; interpretation tentative
items.plain_english: One who is always devoted to dharma and delight, and free from empty anger.

items.question: What devotional attitude marks a person fit to receive the teaching?
premises: Devotion is directed to gods, fire, discipline, and yoginis
Mental serenity accompanies devotion
items.inference: A fit recipient is always serene-minded and devoted to the gods, fire, discipline, and yoginis
items.plain_english: Always serene-minded, with devotion to the gods, fire, discipline, and the yoginis.

items.question: Under what condition should the teacher grant this long-life teaching?
premises: The recipient must be thoroughly examined
The teaching confers long life
items.inference: Only after careful examination should one give this teaching of long life to him
uncertainties: dadyāccirajīvitam is a fused form; object interpretation tentative
items.plain_english: Having always examined him well, one should give to him that which grants long life.

items.question: Who is disqualified by hostility to the yoginis and transgression of the guru's command?
premises: Hostility toward the yoginis is a fault
Violating the guru's command is a fault
items.inference: One hostile to the yoginis and who transgresses the guru's command is disqualified
items.plain_english: And to one hostile to the yoginis, who transgresses the guru's command.

items.question: To whom must the sacred teaching never be given according to this prohibition?
premises: Reviling Shiva is prohibited
Slandering the Kula Bhairava is prohibited
items.inference: The teaching must not be given to a reviler of Shiva or a slanderer of the Kula Bhairava
items.plain_english: Not to one who reviles Shiva, O Goddess, nor to a slanderer of the Kula Bhairava.

items.question: Can even immense material wealth justify giving away this kaula teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents immense wealth
Such wealth might be offered as payment
items.inference: Even one who could accumulate an ocean filled with jewels should not be given it improperly
uncertainties: ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is a fused and unclear form
items.plain_english: Even if one had the means to fill an ocean with jewels...

items.question: What is the status of this kaula teaching across all times?
premises: The teaching is identified as kaula
It is described as a determination for all times
items.inference: This kaula teaching is the definitive determination for all times
items.plain_english: O Great Goddess, this kaula teaching is the definitive determination for all times.

items.question: How should the supreme knowledge be properly given according to this instruction?
premises: Supreme knowledge must be given properly
A specific condition involving seven is indicated
items.inference: The supreme knowledge should be properly given under the stated condition
uncertainties: saptā...ṇnadāpayet is damaged or incomplete in the source
items.plain_english: O Goddess, one should properly give this supreme knowledge... for seven...

items.question: What practice begins first when one engages with the root wheel?
premises: The root wheel is the first focus
Practice proceeds in stages
items.inference: First, when one practices the root wheel, the initial stage begins
uncertainties: yadānyabhyasate is a fused form; segmentation uncertain
items.plain_english: O Beloved, first, when one practices the root wheel...

items.question: What bodily signs mark the first and second stages of this practice?
premises: Practice unfolds in ordered stages
Physical signs accompany these stages
items.inference: First comes trembling, and second comes shaking
items.plain_english: First trembling arises, and shaking is the second.

items.question: What involuntary vocal effect occurs when the practitioner utters all mantras and mudras?
premises: The practitioner engages all mantras and mudras
A spontaneous vocal disturbance arises
items.inference: He indeed utters all the mantras and mudras with stammering speech
uncertainties: durdurapluta is an unusual form; interpretation tentative
items.plain_english: He indeed utters the entire group of mantras and mudras in a stammering way.

items.question: What extraordinary powers over time and form arise in this advanced state?
premises: Advanced practice yields extraordinary effects
Time and form are subject to alteration
items.inference: There arises the deception of time and the transformation of form
items.plain_english: O Goddess, there is the overcoming of time and the transformation of form.
